notes: tex_px: 512 only where detail tells tools apart (Kelly/Crile serrations, Mayo-Hegar jaws and gold rings, the tray); 256 for the rest (2026-10-18 optimisation). category = SurgicalTool.Category: 0 CUTTING, 1 GRASPING, 2 CLAMPING, 3 RETRACTING, 4 SUTURING, 5 OTHER. body: rigid = SurgicalTool in tools/, prop = plain RigidBody3D, static = the tray (both in assets/instruments/). display_name/description/specialities are DRAFTS for clinician review (specialities = SurgicalTool.Speciality: 0 GENERAL, 1 HAND, 2 PLASTIC, 3 SILLY). Source of truth for the set. dims_mm = [length along +Y, width along X, height along Z] in the rest pose; approximate until checked against reference photos. tris = target; ceiling = target * tri_ceiling_factor. phase: 1 = first delivery, 2 = rest of the set, 3 = distractors (silly and lookalike items, docs/distractors.md, built in blend/distractors.blend). scale (optional): the item is built in real mm and shrunk by this factor (silly items 0.65, Julia). ao (optional): bake ambient occlusion into ORM red and darken the albedo by this strength.

t1.note: floor slab 20 mm deep below the tray; walls 100 mm above the rim (invisible containment)
t1.description: Stainless tray the tools are laid out on.

s1.description: #3 handle with a #10 blade: a large curved cutting belly. The classic blade for skin incisions.

s1b.description: #3 handle with a #11 blade: a straight edge running to a sharp triangular point, for stab incisions.

s1c.description: #3 handle with a #15 blade: like a #10 but much smaller, with a short curved belly for small, precise incisions.

s2.description: Heavy straight scissors with short, wide blades and blunt tips. For cutting sutures and tough tissue.

s3.description: Long, slender scissors with short, narrow blades and rounded tips, for delicate dissection. Longer shanks than Mayo scissors.

s4.description: Short (12 cm) forceps with a wide thumb grip that narrows sharply to a fine tip with small teeth. For skin.

s5.description: Long, even forceps with narrow atraumatic tips: fine grooves, no teeth. For vessels and delicate tissue.

s6.description: Hemostat with ring handles and a ratchet lock. Serrations only on the distal half of the jaw: that is how it differs from the Crile.

s6b.description: Hemostat like the Kelly, but the serrations run the whole length of the jaw.

s7.description: Needle holder: gold rings (tungsten-carbide inserts), long shanks and short, heavy jaws. Looks like a clamp, but the jaw is much shorter and wider.

s8.description: Flat, double-ended retractor with a right-angled blade at each end, in two sizes. Held by hand to pull back the wound edges.

m1.description: Round, knurled handle closed by finger pressure, with a fine curved tip. Microsurgery needle holder, no rings.

m2.description: Tiny spring scissors (8.5 cm). The handles spring open and the blades are very short and sharp. Microsurgery.

m4.description: A 1 cm spring clamp that temporarily closes a small vessel during microsurgery.

m5.description: Slim round handle tapering to a fine shaft with a tiny hook at the tip, for lifting fine structures.

m6.description: Round, knurled handle with a collet holding a tiny Beaver blade, for very fine incisions.

t2.note: lobe wall boxes stick out up to 11 mm outside the rim (jam shortcut)
t2.description: Kidney-shaped stainless bowl for used instruments, swabs and fluids.

d1.description: Beauty tweezers with a slanted tip and a painted grip. For eyebrows, not for tissue.

d2.description: Dentist's probe: a ridged handle with a sharp curved hook at each end. It belongs in a dental clinic.

x1.description: A yellow bath duck. It squeaks. Not sterile.

x2.note: tapered ends: the colliders' bounding boxes stick out up to 5.4 mm at the scaled size (the round caps far less)
x2.description: A ripe banana. Curved, but not a retractor.

d3.description: Beauty tool: finger rings and a hinge like a clamp, but the jaws are a wide curved frame with a rubber pad.

d5.description: Red lipstick in a gold case, cap off. Round and knurl-free: not a blade handle.

x3.note: real steel would weigh about 240 g; capped so it doesn't crush the tools
x3.description: Polished steel with a pink jewel. Not a surgical instrument.

x4.note: shrunk from 34 cm (Julia: Oscar about 16 cm, then all silly items 35 % smaller); 80 g like a plastic replica: at 350 g and 150 g the doubled rummage test fails
x4.description: A silver award statuette. Best Supporting Instrument, maybe.

d6.note: real zinc alloy weighs about 220 g; capped like the Oscar
d6.description: Wine opener: two levers rise like wings as the worm screw turns into the cork. Wrong kind of extraction.

d7.description: Battery grooming trimmer with a slotted rotary head. For nostrils, not for sutures.

x5.note: miniature 'pocket edition' (Julia); 250 g: at 150 g the single rummage test threw it out of the tray. Title drawn on the cover by scripts/cover_text.py after every texture bake
x5.description: Dostoevsky's novel, miniature pocket edition. Light reading for a long surgery.

x6.description: A single sock. Where is the other one?
